The second one is safer, but less common. Try the first one, which i am going to explain thoroughtly"_

_"...All we have to do is to bypass the call to nagscreen opening routine. We can't just noop it because it is referenced by the relocation table and the system will try to correct the segment address of the call when it loads the program thus corrupting any instruction we put there and the program will not run. So, we will put a JMP immediately after the call to ShowWindow... ...+ORC's SOLUTION ALSO DOESN'T WORK IN ALL CASES !!! It works if the current date is greater than expiration date or if it is outside the range 1984 to 2049 ! If the current date is lower than the installation date (but it doesn't go below 1984) protection will react - the nagscreen will pop up and the program will terminate."_

8) [+heres' solution](solutions/heressol.htm)  
_"...But near the second address, no conditional jumps are present and breakpointing the first you get a Protection Fault... We have a chance, make a backtrace buffer. So breakpoint the only CS+C8:360F and re-enter your date. You have to establish the buffer range, so type: bpr cs:0000 cs:360F T and re-enter the date. With the SHOW command of SoftICE, you can see:"_

9) [+Aitor's solution](solutions/aitorsol.htm)  
_"...Ripping the encryption code we can write a little program to do the job (it may help in future Micro$oft cracking sessions :)) ... here you got the TP/BASM code (with a few little modifications you can get the C translation)"_

_"...Nuff said about this truly ZEN crack of an intrinsically useless program. Don't ask me why I've done this. I don't know... ...+orc suggested we nop this jump at 8.17e8 out. I don't know whom he is kidding, but certainly noone who's studied his tutorials. Obviously, we \_do\_ want to take that jump, and therefore patch "EB46" for "7246" at 8.17e8."_

please be patient... I'm a neophyte too! :)
First of all, let's give a look to the problems we will have to deal with
(they are the same for msmoney 3.0 and 97):

3) DATE "DELTA" CHECK: the transactions must be below a limit of 60 days for

4) BLANK DATE CHECK: the transactions must have a date in both the versions.

Found it! Here's **+Malattia's HCU Strainer solution** for Microsoft Money, published on Fravia's site as part of the **+HCU (Hacker's Cyber University) 1998** strainer challenge.

## Overview

The strainer required solving 4 parts:
1. Finding MS Money 3 demo (an old program)
2. Explaining why +ORC's MS Project crack method works
3. **Cracking MS Money 3 demo**
4. **Cracking MS Money 97 demo**

The full solution is archived at: **https://www.accessroot.com/fravia/solutions/malatsol.htm**

## Key highlights from Malattia's solution:

### MS Money 3.0 — Date Check at Start
- Used **WinIce** backtracing: `TASK` → `HWND MNYDEMO` → `BMSG` → `STACK` to trace from the error dialog back to the protection code
- Found the date check at `0008:1510` comparing values against `0x5C` (1994) and `0x5E` (1995)
- The date code is calculated by encoding year/month/day into a single word value
- **Patch**: Change `74 11` (je) to `EB 11` (jmp) at `0008:14FE` to always jump to "good guy" code

### MS Money 3.0 — Blank Date & Delta Checks
- Found both checks are near each other at segment `0014`
- **Patch**: Change `74 1D` to `EB 1D` at `0014:2B50` to skip blank date and delta checks

### MS Money 97 — Transaction Date Checks
- Similar approach using SoftIce to trace `MessageBoxA` calls
- Found the blank date check comparing against `FFFF` at `005B5514`
- **Patch**: Change `74 21` to `EB 21` at `005B5508`

### MS Money 97 — End of Evaluation (90 days)
- **Patch**: Change `72 1C` to `EB 1C` at `00470E14` to skip the "expired" check
- Also patches the 15-day warning nag: Change `73 60` to `EB 60` at `0046EB13`

Malattia's approach was notable for combining **live debugging** (WinIce/SoftIce with `HWND`, `BMSG`, `STACK`) with **dead listing** (Wdasm disassembly), and using resource inspection (Borland Resource Workshop, dialog `0x0494`) to identify nag dialogs.
